# Mapping Specification: SUPPORT_TICKETS

**Source file:** data/raw/support_tickets.jsonl
**Data source name:** SUPPORT_TICKETS
**Entity type:** Person
**Generated by:** mapping_workflow

## Field Mappings

| Source Field | Senzing Attribute | Transformation | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ticket_id | RECORD_ID | verbatim | Stable natural key, 100% unique |
| (constant) | DATA_SOURCE | `SUPPORT_TICKETS` | Root attribute |
| (constant) | RECORD_TYPE | `PERSON` | Own feature object; the ticket's subject is the individual requester; no type field (topic is a category) |
| requester_name | NAME_FULL | verbatim | Single name field: not split; nicknames/typos left as-is |
| requester_email | EMAIL_ADDRESS | verbatim | |
| phone | PHONE_NUMBER | verbatim | Three formats in the source; emitted as-is |
| city | ADDR_CITY | verbatim | Same ADDRESS object as postal_code |
| postal_code | ADDR_POSTAL_CODE | verbatim | |
| topic | payload `topic` | verbatim | Ticket category, not used for matching |
| opened_on | payload `opened_on` | verbatim | Two date formats in the source; not used for matching |

The source is sparse (absent values are omitted keys). Blank values are omitted; a feature object is written only when at least one of its attributes is present.


## Mapping Decisions

- One master schema (support_tickets); no child, lookup or relationship schemas; no embedded second entity.
- The profiler's 30 structure variations are combinations of missing keys over the same 8 fields, not distinct record types, so no `--group_by` re-profile.
- Payload keys `topic` and `opened_on` are not registered feature attribute names.
- Cross-source collision check against CRM_CONTACTS and WEB_ORDERS — all pairs exempt, recorded here:
  - NAME: requester_name vs full_name (same quantity) and vs first_name + last_name (parsed vs full); all the record subject.
  - ADDRESS: city/postal_code vs address (parsed vs full) and vs city/zip (same parts); the record subject's location, no usage type on any side.
  - EMAIL: requester_email vs email (the record subject's email); PHONE: phone vs phone.

## Quality Notes

- Source quality score 75.5 (Acceptable, 70-79 band; the bootcamper accepted the gaps at Phase 1 and chose to proceed to loading). Output population equals source presence: NAME 97.2%, EMAIL 80.5%, ADDRESS 76.7% (city 50.1%, postal 53.7%), PHONE 51.1%.
- 42 records (2.8%) carry no name; addresses have no street, so they are a weak matching signal.
- sz_json_analyzer.py: no errors or warnings (1,500 records). sz_verbatim_check.py: all values verbatim. sz_routing_report.py: only ticket_id listed as dropped (it is RECORD_ID).
- Structurally validated; semantic validation happens at Data processing's match-key audit.
